title: Autopilot enrollment fails when depot asset tag contains non-ASCII characters (JSON parse error on MDM registration)
text:
Autopilot enrollment fails when depot asset tag contains non-ASCII characters (JSON parse error on MDM registration)

description:
Issue summary:
Depot-repaired devices are failing Autopilot/Intune enrollment during MDM registration. Devices provision in the depot, the asset-tagger writes the asset tag into system metadata. If the asset tag contains non-ASCII characters (accented letters, emojis, or copy-paste artifacts), Intune's registration endpoint returns a 400 and the local enrollment client logs a JSON parse error.

Impact:
- Blocks automated re-enrollment for depot-repaired machines (approx. 18 devices reported across two days).
- Manual intervention required to complete Autopilot profile application (IT must re-enroll or sanitize asset tag).
- Delays device return to service and increases depot turnaround.

Environment:
- Windows 11 22H2 build used by Autopilot profile; corporate Autopilot + Intune flow; depot asset tag scanner v2.1.
- Failures observed in us-west and us-east provisioning depots.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Depot imaging process runs and asset-tag scanner writes serial + user-supplied asset tag into system metadata (UEFI variable and inventory DB).
2) Device reboots and Autopilot client attempts enrollment (login.microsoftonline.com + Intune MDM registration).
3) Intune returns HTTP 400 with body indicating invalid JSON. On device: Enrollment fails with local client error: "Failed to parse enrollment payload: Unexpected token at position 12".

Observed logs / snippets:
- Device-side (C:\Windows\Temp\autopilot.log): "MDM registration failed: 400 Bad Request - Payload parse error: invalid character '\\u2019' in string literal"
- Intune-side (ingest logs): "POST /enrollments - requestId=abc123 - status=400 - error=InvalidJSON - field=assetTag"
- Asset DB: asset_tag entries for affected hosts include non-ASCII characters (e.g., "MGR–50É", "LF-12🚀").

Notes:
- Not all non-ASCII chars cause failure; seems related to UTF-8 vs Windows-1252 encoding when the depot scanner writes the UEFI variable.
- Affected machines share a depot scanner firmware revision deployed last month.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: asset tag sanitization defect in depot scanner producing an encoding mismatch when writing UEFI variable. Collected 8 affected devices and captured UEFI variable values vs inventory DB copy. Observed escape sequences and unexpected 0x92 byte in some entries (Windows-1252 smart quote).

Actions taken:
- Pulled scanner logs and reproduction on bench: confirmed scanner emits UTF-8 on stdout but the UEFI write helper converts to system codepage (windows-1252) producing invalid JSON when the backend expects strict UTF-8.
- Reproduced enrollment failure against a staging Intune endpoint using an isolated VM and injected asset tags containing smart quotes and emoji; confirmed 400 responses matching production failures.
- Cross-checked with asset normalization microservice: current validation only strips whitespace and restricts to 1-64 chars, but does not normalize to ASCII or perform NFKC normalization.
- Looked for related tickets: linked INT-50321 (serial normalization / assetdb mismatch) for background on assetdb rules.

root_cause:
Depot asset-tag scanner and UEFI write helper perform inconsistent encoding conversions (windows-1252 bytes written where Intune expects UTF-8). This resulted in non-ASCII bytes in the asset_tag field that cause Intune's registration JSON validation to fail.

workaround:
Depot Ops applied a temporary input validation on the scanner UI to block non-ASCII characters and instructed techs to sanitize existing asset tags. For devices already stuck: manual wipe and re-enroll after sanitizing the asset tag UEFI variable (scripts provided).

resolution_plan:
Short term: roll out asset-normalizer hotfix (v1.4.1) to canonicalize asset tags (NFKC normalize, remove emoji, replace smart quotes with ASCII equivalents) and add server-side strict UTF-8 validation. Medium term: update depot scanner and UEFI write helper to ensure UTF-8 is preserved when writing variables; add automated test for non-ASCII asset tags in CI.

Deployment steps:
- Merge PR for asset-normalizer (PR #42) and canary deploy to us-west (2026-03-14).
- Monitor enrollment success rate and error rates on Intune ingestion logs for 72h.
- Release depot scanner patch (v2.1.3) with corrected UEFI write logic and roll to all depots (target 2026-03-21).
- Add telemetry and lint rule to depot agent that rejects non-ASCII and surfaces immediate validation error to operator.

resolution_notes:
In-progress: asset-normalizer v1.4.1 hotfix merged (PR #42), canary in us-west started 2026-03-14 03:00 UTC; initial canary devices show successful enrollment. Depot scanner patch prepared and scheduled for next week. Manual remediation script published to Confluence for depot techs to correct existing devices.

next_steps:
1) Finish canary monitoring for v1.4.1 (Marcus). 2) Roll out depot scanner v2.1.3 (Depot Ops). 3) Run remediation sweep on devices imaged in last 30 days and re-attempt enrollment for ones with sanitized tags (Support + Depot Ops).
